donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

It is critical that we continue to work together to advance the infrastructure in our district and ensure that Virginians have access to safe, reliable, and convenient roads. Read more at https://t.co/m0hU55nXeC.

It was a pleasure meeting with Taylor Tugwell, a 2026 Angels in Adoption honoree, to hear about her experiences and commitment to supporting children and families. Thank you, Taylor, for sharing your story and for your dedication to making a difference! https://t.co/LGZMVqJrAT

@EPA and @NFWFnews announced over $90 million for Chesapeake Bay watershed restoration projects, including critical investments in the First District. These projects will restore oyster reefs, protect shorelines along the Rappahannock River, and improve fish habitats. As vice chair of the House Natural Resources Committee, I will continue advocating for investments that protect our waterways, support local watermen, and preserve the Bay for future generations. Read more here: https://t.co/V5O030JN8V

Parents should have the freedom to choose the education that best fits their children. I enjoyed meeting with homeschool families in Henrico to discuss strengthening education, supporting parents, and ensuring every student has the opportunity to succeed. https://t.co/d3y27rg7Q0

Virginia’s First District is home to world-class research facilities and critical military installations that play an essential role in our economic and national security. It was a pleasure to welcome Deputy Secretary of Energy James Danly to the First District to showcase the groundbreaking work being done at Jefferson Lab and discuss the importance of reliable, resilient energy infrastructure at Naval Weapons Station Yorktown. From investing in scientific innovation to modernizing our military installations, we must ensure that our nation has the technology, infrastructure, and resources necessary to remain competitive and maintain a strong national defense.

I enjoyed sitting down with Chesterfield County’s new County Administrator, Dr. Kevin Catlin, to welcome him to the community and hear about his priorities for the county. I look forward to working together to support Chesterfield’s continued growth and ensure it remains a great place to live, work, and raise a family.

Expanding access to high-quality, affordable health care remains one of my top priorities. I enjoyed touring Richmond Heart and Vascular Associates and learning more about how their cardiac surgery center is providing advanced cardiac care to patients in Hanover and surrounding communities.

"The Pentagon and the Army need to move fast. They need to experiment rapidly, identify failures early, learn from them and incorporate those lessons before flawed approaches are scaled across the force." Read more here: https://t.co/E3pBfO2vDr

I appreciated meeting with leaders from the Jewish Community Federation of Richmond to hear about their priorities and discuss issues important to the Jewish community. Thank you for the thoughtful conversation and continued engagement. https://t.co/3Uk71soRTZ

It was great joining the Richmond region’s rising leaders at the ICONS Awards pre-party! Congratulations to this year’s finalists, and thank you for your leadership and commitment to making a difference across our communities. https://t.co/BQClG1X8o9

Do you need help with checking on Social Security benefits, renewing a passport, or processing a VA claim? My district offices in Glen Allen and Yorktown are open every day, but my team is also hosting mobile office hours in Tappahannock tomorrow to assist constituents with casework. Sign up: https://t.co/r2w5edeTEh

I am committed to protecting Americans’ Second Amendment rights and am honored to have recently received a Dean’s List Recognition from @NSSF. I believe it is necessary to protect an individual’s fundamental right to keep and bear arms. We must be deliberate in improving public safety while ensuring that we defend citizens' constitutional rights to purchase, possess, and use firearms for lawful purposes. I will continue working in Congress to defend our constitutional freedoms. Thank you to NSSF for this recognition. Read more here: https://t.co/JHYRbxyoRR
Happy birthday to the @USNavy! Join me in celebrating 251 years of incredible service, and thank you to the brave men and women who defend our nation at sea. https://t.co/S2pNj4PcKm

Strong federal and local partnerships are critical to advancing economic development across the Middle Peninsula. I appreciated joining the Middle Peninsula Planning District Commission and U.S. Economic Development Administration to discuss federal resources, grant opportunities, and ways we can work together to support infrastructure, workforce development, and economic growth across the region.

Thank you to the team at Chesterfield Mental Health Support Services for showing me how they are working to meet behavioral health needs across the community. We had a productive discussion about expanding access to care, strengthening the behavioral health workforce, and ensuring those experiencing a mental health crisis can get the support they need.

Every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that cannot be used to provide care for Americans who rely on Medicaid. I am proud to join my colleagues in introducing the HELP STATES Act to give states a stronger incentive to identify and recover fraudulent payments while ensuring those recovered funds are reinvested in protecting the integrity of the Medicaid program. We owe it to taxpayers and Medicaid enrollees to safeguard these resources and hold those who defraud the system accountable. Read more here: https://t.co/smKw4SfTm3

Small businesses are the backbone of our communities. I am honored to receive the Guardian of Small Business Award  from the National Federation of Independent Business for my work to support Main Street businesses. I am proud to advance policies that cut taxes, reduce burdensome regulations, and make it easier for small businesses to create jobs and invest in their communities. I will continue working to ensure our small businesses have the tools they need to succeed. Read more here: https://t.co/UW6xzGDtjU

Virginia’s working waterfronts are an important part of our economy and way of life. I enjoyed visiting Rappahannock Oyster Co. to learn more about their operations and discuss supporting our aquaculture industry, strengthening rural economies, and protecting the Chesapeake Bay. https://t.co/DgXFl9CYGA

Today marks three years since the horrific October 7 terrorist attack against Israel. We must always remember the innocent lives lost that day and in the days that followed and recommit ourselves to standing against antisemitism and terrorism in all its forms. I am grateful that all of the hostages are home, and I will always stand with our ally Israel and the Jewish people.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
